_about.note: Evidence category of every number used by the Prompt 11 voice part: CommsStage (scripts/voice/comms_stage.gd), VoiceRouter (voice_router.gd), VoiceScheduler (voice_scheduler.gd) and VoiceService (voice_service.gd). Categories: contract (fixed by the project brief), balance (game tuning), engineering (software behaviour, chosen and tested in this project), physics (general physics, not from the source register). No number here is NASA data. The radio delay is fiction: a damaged 2080 radio's buffering, not a measured radio figure, not network delay and not Earth-Mars light time.

CommsStage.DELAY_S.note: Stage 0 no exterior link; stages 1-4: 30 s, 15 s, 5 s, near-immediate (0 s intentional). From the brief's communications paragraph and Prompt 11.

CommsStage.CARD_PARTS.note: Cards comms_radio_1..4 cost 1, 2, 3, 4 spare parts (worker specification for Prompt 11).

comms_radio tiers.note: Energy level needed by comms_radio_1..4: 0, 1, 2, 3, so the first link is available early (the tutorial's communications stage) and later repairs follow the colony's electrical learning.

VoiceRouter.FULL_M.note: Indoor speech at full level through 5 m.

VoiceRouter.SILENT_M.note: Indoor speech fades to zero by 25 m (smoothstep between 5 and 25 m: 0.5 at 15 m).

VoiceRouter.DOOR_FACTOR.note: Speech through one open door is at half the level of the same path length in one room (about -6 dB), scaled by how far the door is open. Not an acoustic measurement.

VoiceRouter.DOOR_OPEN_MIN.note: A door less than 5 % open counts as closed (closed doors are silent).

VoiceRouter.PORTAL_PROBE_M.note: A door's two zones are sampled 0.6 m either side of the door line.

VoiceScheduler.FRAME_SAMPLES.note: 960 samples = 20 ms per Opus frame (the TwoVoIP helper's default frame length).

VoiceScheduler.JITTER_S.note: 80 ms reorder window after the intended schedule: one 20 ms capture frame, one 16 ms game frame and about 44 ms of network jitter. Applied after the intentional delay, never instead of it.

VoiceScheduler.PLAYBACK_TARGET_S.note: A player starts when 40 ms (two frames) are queued, so frames released at game-frame steps do not run dry.

VoiceScheduler.MAX_QUEUE_S.note: At most 40 s of audio waiting per speaker: more than the longest delay (30 s) plus room for queued speech behind it.

VoiceScheduler.MAX_QUEUE_FRAMES.note: 2000 frames = 40 s of 20 ms frames per speaker.

VoiceScheduler.MAX_UTTERANCES.note: At most 16 utterances waiting per speaker; the oldest whole one is dropped (with a note) beyond that.

VoiceScheduler.MAX_TOTAL_FRAMES.note: 6000 frames for all speakers together (three other players at the per-speaker bound).

VoiceScheduler.STALL_S.note: An utterance that receives nothing for 1 s while it waits for a packet is ended (the speaker left or the network broke).

VoiceScheduler.MAX_UTTERANCE_FRAMES.note: 3000 frames = 60 s; a longer hold of V becomes several utterances, which keeps frame numbers in 16 bits and every buffer bounded.

VoiceService.OPUS_BITRATE.note: 24 kbit/s Opus voice (about 3 kB/s per speaker plus headers).

VoiceService.MIC_HANG_S.note: The microphone stays open 3 s after V is released so quick presses do not keep reopening it.

VoiceService.MIC_SIGNAL_TIMEOUT_S.note: An open microphone with no samples for 3 s is reported as no signal.

VoiceService.MIC_TARGET_PEAK.note: Auto-gain lifts speech toward a 0.6 peak (2026-11-15: players' microphones were far too quiet).

VoiceService.MIC_MAX_GAIN.note: Auto-gain boosts a quiet microphone by at most 16x (+24 dB).

VoiceService.MIC_START_GAIN.note: Auto-gain starts at 6x so the first words are already audible.

VoiceService.MIC_SPEECH_FLOOR.note: Below a 0.004 peak a chunk is room silence: the gain holds instead of pumping up hiss.

VoiceService.MIC_GAIN_RISE.note: The gain rises 3% of the way to its target per 20 ms chunk (about 0.7 s) and drops at once.

VoiceService.MIC_KNEE.note: Soft limiter above 0.7 so boosted shouts never clip.

VoiceService.LOW_INPUT_RATE_HZ.note: An input at 16 kHz or less is a Bluetooth device in call mode; the player is told to switch the input and restart.

VoiceService.MOUTH_HEIGHT_M.note: Indoor speech comes from 1.6 m above the speaker's feet.

Earth-Mars light time.note: Shown only as words (many minutes, depending on where the planets are). Radio waves travel at the speed of light; the Earth-Mars distance changes over the planets' orbits. Not taken from the source register, and the game computes nothing from it.
